headline: This 2017 law creates a one-time exception that lets the first Secretary of Defense appointed after its enactment be a former regular officer who left active duty at least three years earlier.
what_it_does: Federal law normally bars anyone from being appointed Secretary of Defense within seven years after leaving active duty as a regular commissioned officer. This law allows the first person appointed to the post after its enactment to be someone who is at least three years past that active-duty date. The exception applies only to that first appointment.

who_it_affects.group: Retired regular commissioned officers of the Armed Forces who might be considered for Secretary of Defense
who_it_affects.how: Someone who left regular active duty three to seven years before a future appointment could be eligible for the first appointment under this exception, although the normal seven-year limit still applies to everyone else.

when_it_takes_effect: On enactment, January 20, 2017, and it applies only to the first Secretary of Defense appointed after that date.
